object.title: Dikranjan's conjecture on the coarsest Hausdorff topology of permutation groups
object.statement:
Let $X$ be an infinite set, and let $G$ be a subgroup of $S(X)$ such that $S_{\omega}(X)\subset G$. The topology of pointwise convergence on $G$ is the coarsest Hausdorff group topology on $G$.

**Dikranjan's conjecture.** The topology of pointwise convergence is the coarsest Hausdorff group topology on $G$.

The conjecture concerns algebraically determined topologies on permutation groups. The paper confirms it by proving the stated coarseness result, so the conjecture is solved.
object.source_name: Taras Banakh, Igor Guran and Igor Protasov, “Algebraically determined topologies on permutation groups”, arXiv:1201.0087 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.0087

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2012); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: Cyclically distinct composition interpretation for the leafed-cycle cone
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}_n$ be the cone constrained by the Laplacian minor of a leafed $n$-cycle, and let $\lambda=(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_{n-1})$ be an integer point of $\mathcal{C}_n$. For a non-negative integer $m$, consider the integer points with first coordinate $\lambda_0=m$.

**Cyclically distinct composition conjecture.** The number of integer points $\lambda\in\mathcal{C}_n$ with $\lambda_0=m$ is equal to the number of compositions of $m$ into $n$ parts that are cyclically distinct.

This conjecture would provide a combinatorial interpretation for the coefficients of $\sigma_{\mathcal{C}_n}(q)$.
object.source_name: Benjamin Braun, Robert Davis, Ashley Harrison, Jessica McKim, Jenna Noll and Clifford Taylor, “Compositions constrained by graph Laplacian minors”, arXiv:1202.2013 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.2013

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2012).

object.title: The minor inequality facet conjecture for circulant set covering polyhedra
object.statement:
Let $C_n^k$ be a circulant matrix, let $W\subset\mathbb Z_n$ define a relevant circulant minor isomorphic to $C_{n'}^{k'}$, and let $Q(C_n^k)$ denote the associated set covering polyhedron. The corresponding minor inequality is

$$
\sum_{i\in W}2x_i+\sum_{i\notin W}x_i\geq\left\lceil\frac{n'}{k'}\right\rceil.
$$

Here, $W$ is relevant when $n'\neq0\pmod {k'}$ and $\left\lceil n'/k'\right\rceil>\left\lceil n/k\right\rceil$. **The minor inequality facet conjecture.** A relevant minor inequality corresponding to a minor of $C_n^k$ isomorphic to $C_{n'}^{k'}$ defines a facet of $Q(C_n^k)$ if and only if $n'=1\pmod {k'}$. The conjecture seeks a complete characterization of when these non-boolean, non-rank inequalities are facet defining; the supplied source gives no evidence of resolution.
object.source_name: Silvia M. Bianchi, Graciela L. Nasini and Paola B. Tolomei, “The Minor inequalities in the description of the Set Covering Polyhedron of Circulant Matrices”, arXiv:1206.1300 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.1300

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2012).

object.title: The even-cycle decomposition conjecture for odd-$K_5$-minor-free signed graphs
object.statement: A signed graph is a graph whose edges are designated even or odd; a cycle is **even** when it contains an even number of odd edges. A graph is **even cycle decomposable** if its edge set can be partitioned into even cycles. The graph is **Eulerian** if every vertex has even degree, and **odd-$K_5$-minor free** if it has no odd minor of $K_5$. **Even-cycle decomposition conjecture.** Every $2$-connected Eulerian loopless odd-$K_5$-minor-free signed graph with an even number of odd edges is even cycle decomposable. This conjecture extends the known results for bipartite graphs and graphs with no $K_5$-minor, where the corresponding necessary conditions are sufficient for an even-cycle decomposition.

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

object.title: Brockman–Kay conjecture on intersecting families of multisets
object.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $M(n,k)$ be the $k\times n$ rectangle representation of $k$-multisets, and let $\mathcal{M}(n,k,t)$ denote the families of $t$-intersecting $k$-multisets of $[n]$. **Brockman–Kay conjecture.** There is $n_0(k,t)$ such that if $n\geq n_0(k,t)$ and $\mathcal{F}\in\mathcal{M}(n,k,t)$, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq\binom{n+k-t-1}{k-t}.
$$

Furthermore, equality is achieved if and only if every member of $\mathcal{F}$ contains a fixed $t$-multiset of $M(n,k)$. This conjecture concerns the extremal size of $t$-intersecting multiset families; the paper records a later result establishing the bound under the explicit threshold $n\geq t(k-t)+2$, while the equality characterization is given in the corresponding threshold conjecture.
object.source_name: Zoltán Füredi, Dániel Gerbner and Máté Vizer, “A discrete isodiametric result: the Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem for multisets”, arXiv:1212.1071 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1071

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2012).

object.title: Meagher–Purdy conjecture on intersecting families of multisets
object.statement:
Let $k,n,t$ be positive integers with $t\leq k$, let $M(n,k)$ be the rectangle representation of $k$-multisets, and let $\mathcal{M}(n,k,t)$ denote the families of $t$-intersecting $k$-multisets of $[n]$. **Meagher–Purdy conjecture.** If

$$
t(k-t)+2\leq n
$$

and $\mathcal{F}\in\mathcal{M}(n,k,t)$, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq\binom{n+k-t-1}{k-t}.
$$

Moreover, if $n>t(k-t)+2$, equality holds if and only if every member of $\mathcal{F}$ contains a fixed $t$-multiset of $M(n,k)$. This gives the paper’s proposed explicit threshold for the multiset Erdős–Ko–Rado bound; the paper’s abstract states that the numerical bound is established for this threshold, while the full equality assertion is the conjectural part recorded here.
object.source_name: Zoltán Füredi, Dániel Gerbner and Máté Vizer, “A discrete isodiametric result: the Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem for multisets”, arXiv:1212.1071 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1071

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2012).

object.title: The order bound conjecture for critical graphs
object.statement:
A graph is **critical** with tree-depth $k$ if its tree-depth is $k$ and every proper minor has smaller tree-depth. The order of a graph is its number of vertices.

**The order bound conjecture.** Every critical graph with tree-depth $k$ has at most

$$
2^{k-1}
$$

vertices.

The conjecture appears in work of Dvořák, Giannopoulou, and Thilikos, where its original form also includes induced-subgraph-critical graphs. The paper establishes partial results toward the bound; the general statement remains open.
object.source_name: Michael D. Barrus and John Sinkovic, “Uniqueness and minimal obstructions for tree-depth”, arXiv:1310.1116 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.1116

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2013).

object.title: Strengthening of the Schrijver graph quadrangulation theorem
object.statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be integers with $n>2k\geq 2$, and let $SG(n,k)$ denote the Schrijver graph. A **quadrangulation** of $P^{n-2k}$ is a graph embedded in the projective space $P^{n-2k}$ so that every face is a quadrilateral; it is **non-bipartite** if its graph is not bipartite. A spanning subgraph contains all vertices of $SG(n,k)$. **Schrijver graph quadrangulation conjecture.** The Schrijver graph $SG(n,k)$ contains a non-bipartite quadrangulation of $P^{n-2k}$ as a spanning subgraph. This would strengthen the stated theorem, which constructs a non-bipartite quadrangulation of $P^{n-2k}$ admitting a homomorphism into $SG(n,k)$; whether the stronger spanning-subgraph assertion holds is left as an open question.

object.references:

object.title: Conjectured circular-flow bound for odd-regular graphs
object.statement:
Let $t>1$ be an integer and let $G$ be a $(2t+1)$-graph, meaning a graph in which every vertex has degree $2t+1$. **The odd-regular flow conjecture.** Every such graph satisfies

$$
F_c(G)\leq 2+\frac{2}{t}.
$$

object.title: Ramsey expansion conjecture for finite-signature homogeneous structures
object.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a homogeneous structure with a finite relational signature. An **expansion** of $\Gamma$ is a structure obtained by adding relations to its signature; its age is the class of finite structures embeddable into it. **Ramsey expansion conjecture.** Then $\Gamma$ has a homogeneous expansion by finitely many relations whose age has the Ramsey property. This conjecture asks whether the finite relational expansions that are known to occur typically can always be found; it is motivated by the connection between Ramsey classes, homogeneous structures, and structural Ramsey theory, and the source presents it as an open question.

object.title: Wu–Hong revised conjecture on deep holes of primitive Reed–Solomon codes
object.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field, let $D=\mathbb{F}_q^*$ be the evaluation set of a primitive Reed–Solomon code with code length $n=q-1$, dimension $k$, and codebook $\mathcal{C}$. Let $u$ be a received word represented by its interpolating polynomial $u(x)$. A word is a **deep hole** when $d(u,\mathcal{C})=n-k$. **Wu–Hong revised conjecture.** All deep holes for primitive Reed–Solomon codes are those words $u$ represented by

$$
u(x)=a x^k+v(x) \quad\text{or}\quad u(x)=a x^{q-2}+v(x),
$$

where $a\ne 0$ and $\deg(v(x))\leq k-1$. The second family is known to consist of deep holes, and the conjecture revises the Cheng–Murray claim in light of that family; the full classification remains open in the stated generality.
object.source_name: Matt Keti and Daqing Wan, “Deep Holes in Reed-Solomon Codes Based on Dickson Polynomials”, arXiv:1507.01653 (2016).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2015). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1309.3546](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.3546).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.01653

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

object.title: Well-quasi-ordering conjecture for finite-tree-width graphs
object.statement: Let a graph have **finite tree-width** if its tree-width is finite, and consider the minor relation on graphs. **Finite-tree-width well-quasi-ordering conjecture.** The graphs of finite tree-width are well-quasi-ordered under the minor relation. This is presented as an even stronger conjecture motivated by the fact that known counterexamples to well-quasi-ordering infinite graphs do not have finite tree-width. Its status is refuted according to the supplied evidence.

object.title: Sumner's conjecture for oriented trees
object.statement:
Let $T$ be an oriented tree, let $n=|V(T)|$ be its order, and let $\operatorname{unvd}(T)$ denote its unavoidability.

**Sumner's conjecture.** Every oriented tree of order $n>1$ is $(2n-2)$-unavoidable; equivalently,

$$
\operatorname{unvd}(T)\leqslant 2n-2.
$$

This is a celebrated conjecture about tournaments and oriented trees. The source does not state a resolution, so its status remains open.

object.title: Aharoni-Berger conjecture for graphs
object.statement:
Let $M_1,\dots,M_n$ be matchings of size $n$ in a graph. A **rainbow matching** is a matching whose edges can be assigned distinct indices $i$ so that each edge belongs to $M_i$.

**Aharoni-Berger conjecture.** Every collection of $n$ matchings of size $n$ in a graph admits a rainbow matching of size $n-1$.

This drops the bipartiteness requirement from the preceding conjecture. The $n-1$ bound is best possible, as shown by the cycle construction described in the source, but the general assertion remains open in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Candida Bowtell, Andrea Freschi, Gal Kronenberg and Jun Yan, “A note on improved bounds for hypergraph rainbow matching problems”, arXiv:2501.03216 (2025).

object.title: Graph isomorphism conjectures for edge-, spanning-tree-, and subset-deleted graphs
object.statement: Let $G,H,G_a,G_b$ be graphs, let $E_G\subset E(G)$ and $E_H\subset E(H)$ be edge subsets, let $T_a,T_b$ be spanning trees, and let $S_G\in V(G)\cup E(G)$ and $S_H\in V(H)\cup E(H)$ be proper subsets. **Graph isomorphism conjectures.** (i) If $|E_G|=|E_H|$, $G-E_G\cong H-E_H$, and $G,H$ are connected $(p,q)$-graphs admitting the isomorphic subgraph similarity, then $G\cong H$ by Kelly–Ulam's Reconstruction Conjecture. (ii) If each spanning tree $T_a$ of a connected $(p,q)$-graph $G_a$ corresponds to a spanning tree $T_b$ of another connected graph $G_b$ with $T_a\cong T_b$, and vice versa, then $G_a\cong G_b$. (iii) If $G$ and $H$ have $n$ vertices and each proper subset $S_G\in V(G)\cup E(G)$ corresponds to a proper subset $S_H\in V(H)\cup E(H)$ with $G-S_G\cong H-S_H$, then $G\cong H$. These proposed extensions of reconstruction from deleted subgraphs concern when graph isomorphism is determined by families of edge-, spanning-tree-, or subset-deleted graphs; the source gives no resolution status.

object.references:

object.title: Conjecture on the listed poly-depth dualities between commuting Pauli models and classical interaction models
object.statement:
The paper considers commuting Pauli Hamiltonians and polynomial-depth quantum circuits implementing dualities between such Hamiltonians and classical interaction models. The listed dualities are described as arising from deterministic polynomial-time tableau diagonalization and empirical patterns in the resulting Hamiltonians.

**Poly-depth duality conjecture.** The poly-depth dualities listed in the table hold in the sense of the paper's definition of duality.

The conjecture asserts the validity of the eight empirically identified dualities, including dualities to one-dimensional Ising chains. Establishing these dualities would support efficient Gibbs-state preparation by reducing sampling to simpler classical state-preparation problems followed by an efficient quantum circuit; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or refuted.

object.title: The spectral conjecture for detection in random geometric graphs
object.statement:
Let $
obreak\boldsymbol{x}_1,
obreak\ldots,
obreak\boldsymbol{x}_n$ be latent points on the sphere, and let 
$$
be the normalized kernel operator on the sphere associated with the random geometric graph (RGG) kernel. Write
$$
 for the trace of the cube of this operator.

**Spectral detection conjecture.** The sharp threshold for distinguishing the RGG from its Erdős–Rényi counterpart is determined by

$$
n^3\operatorname{tr}^2(\kappa^3)=1.
$$

Equivalently, the detectable regime should satisfy $n^3\operatorname{tr}^2(\kappa^3)\gg1$, while the undetectable regime should satisfy $n^3\operatorname{tr}^2(\kappa^3)\ll1$.

The conjecture is motivated by both the signed triangle statistic and the Kullback–Leibler expansion, where $\operatorname{tr}(\kappa^3)$ arises naturally. It unifies the conjectured threshold for hard RGGs with the proved thresholds for several smooth-kernel models, but the general sharp characterization remains open.
object.source_name: Cheng Mao, Yihong Wu and Jiaming Xu, “Random geometric graphs with smooth kernels: sharp detection threshold and a spectral conjecture”, arXiv:2602.14998 (2026).

object.title: Carlet–Lou weight-spectrum conjecture for Reed–Muller codes
object.statement:
Let $RM(r,m)$ denote the Reed–Muller code of order $r$ in $m$ variables, and let its weight spectrum be the set of Hamming weights of its codewords. For a set $S$ of weights, write $\overline{S}=\{2^m-s\mid s\in S\}$. Let $c$ be any positive integer and suppose that $m\geq 2c$. **Carlet–Lou weight-spectrum conjecture.** The weight spectrum of $RM(m-c,m)$ has the form

$$
\{0\}\cup A\cup B\cup C\cup \overline{B}\cup \overline{A}\cup \{2^m\},
$$

where $A\subseteq[2^c,2^{c+1}]$ is the set given by Kasami and Tokura, $B\subseteq[2^{c+1},2^{c+1}+2^{c-1}]$ is the set given by Kasami, Tokura, and Azumi, and $C\subseteq[2^{c+1}+2^{c-1},2^m-2^{c+1}-2^{c-1}]$ consists of all consecutive even integers. The sets $\overline{A}$ and $\overline{B}$ are the complements of $A$ and $B$, respectively, with respect to $2^m$. This conjecture proposes a general description of the weight spectrum of high-order Reed–Muller codes; the cited descriptions of $A$ and $B$ come from earlier work, while the asserted complete form remains an open question.
object.source_name: Milo Leuenberger and Manuel Albrizzio, “On the Weight Spectrum of the Reed-Muller Codes RM(7,14)”, arXiv:2606.21425 (2026).
object.references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2026).

object.title: Tightness conjecture for the rooted $K_{3,3}$ minor bound
object.statement: The preceding theorem gives a bound on rooted $K_{3,3}$ minors; denote this bound by the quantity appearing in Theorem. **Tightness conjecture.** The bound in Theorem is tight. This conjecture asserts that the bound cannot be improved and is presented as a possible starting point for determining forbidden minor characterizations related to reducibility. The source does not provide evidence resolving its status.
